To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the parasitic reactances resulting from the discontinuities in coupled-stripline broadband multisection directional couplers, high-pass tapered line directional couplers, magic-T's, and phase shifters can be substantially reduced, and thus, the return losses and isolation can be improved, by introducing compensating capacitances in the cross sections of coupled lines and signal lines.

the broadband multisections coupled-line circuits can be designed with very high return losses and isolation, and with very low insertion losses, if the parasitic reactances are reduced or compensated.

broadband coupled-line circuits can be designed by using the proposed equivalent circuit and the proposed broadband compensation techniques, and that the broadband coupled-line circuits designed by using the presented techniques have better performances than the circuits designed by using other techniques.

the problem of discontinuites in broadband multisections coupled-stripline directional couplers, magic-T's, phase shifters and tapered-line 3 dB couplers.
the development of broadband and ultra-broadwidth coupled-stripline circuitry.
the problem of discontinuies in coupled-line circuits and their compensation.

the broadband coupled-stripline circuit design problem is not only the design of a number of sections of coupled and terminating lines but also the design of the connections between them.

, in order to achieve broadband and/or ultra-broadband performance for coupled-stripline couplers, phase shifter, and magic-T, it is essential to compensate the discontinuities resulting from the connections of the signal and coupled lines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for the first time, a systematic design procedure has been developed and presented in two papers for broadband multisection directional couplers, broadband phase shifters, broadband and ultra-broadwidth high-pass directional couplers, magic-T's, and other circuits, which are constructed by means of broadband coupled-stripline lines.

the proposed technique of compensation of the effects of the connections of signal lines to the coupled-line sections is very efficient in reducing the parasitic effects and improving the performance of broadband coupled-line circuits.
the proposed broadband compensation method has been successfully applied in the design of broadband and ultra-broadwidth coupled-line circuits with high performance and low cost
The main takeaway from our work is that
broadband coupled-stripline directional couplers, magic-T's, and phase shifters can be efficiently designed by using the proposed compensation technique.

the broadband multisections directional couplers and phase shifters can be designed with a high degree of accuracy, and with the same accuracy, the ultra-broadband directional couplers can be designed.
the broadband compensation technique is very effective for improving the performances of the broadband coupled-stripline directional couplers, magic-T's, and phase shifters.
